description: Predicting how molecules interact is central to drug discovery: it offers important information about how a new drug might work in the human body, the side effects it can cause and more. Computationally modeling these interactions can reduce the need for lengthy and expensive lab work, but some interactions still remain beyond the reach of classical computers.
title: Quantum software matches classical benchmark for a molecular interaction

description: An international team led by researchers from Senckenberg am Meer in Wilhelmshaven has described two new species of marine tardigrades. The tiny marine organisms were discovered in the sediment of the Senghor Seamount off the coast of Cape Verde. According to the researchers, the discovery underscores the role of undersea mountains as oases of biodiversity. The study, which includes comprehensive taxonomic descriptions of the new species, has been published in the journal "ZooKeys."
title: The call of the seamount: Two new armored tardigrades described in the Atlantic

description: New research about condensates—cellular compartments that act as hubs for facilitating biological reactions—continues to reveal novel insights into how cells function. Among those continuing to push the field forward are members of the Marine Biological Laboratory's condensate consortium, including Amy Gladfelter, a professor at Duke University and current co-director of the MBL physiology course, and former MBL physiology course student and past MBL Whitman fellow Dragomir Milovanovic, a professor at the Charité Berlin University Institute of Biochemistry.
title: Broadening the role of RNA: A messenger, a mediator and now a condensate coordinator

description: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.
title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer

description: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.
title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years

description: The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation.
title: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist

description: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north.
title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions

description: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).
title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors

description: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.
title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users

description: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before.
title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms

description: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.
title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts

description: Scientists at Texas A&M AgriLife Research, a member of The Texas A&M University System, have developed a hemp plant that produces no detectable cannabinoids, including THC.
title: New hemp plant produces no detectable THC, potentially reducing risk of crop destruction

description: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model can detect stress in agricultural crops using a nondestructive imaging technique, allowing changes in crop health to be monitored over time. Developed by a team of researchers at Penn State, the new model shows promise for accurately detecting crop stress caused by drought, disease, nutrient deficiency and other causes while using less computing power than some existing AI methods.
title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations

description: A research team at the University of Potsdam has conducted a field experiment to investigate whether contact through social media can reduce prejudice. The findings suggest that following an unfamiliar Instagram profile for just three days can lead to more favorable attitudes—not only toward the group represented by the profile. The study was published in the Journal of the Association for Information Systems.
title: Can Instagram reduce prejudice? Study reveals the potential and limits of social media contact

description: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb.
title: A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells

description: As the climate warms, thousands of glacial lakes are growing behind potentially unstable natural dams. Despite the potential risk of flooding to communities downstream, these lakes remain outside formal safety regulation.
title: Hazardous glacial lakes need reservoir-style safety oversight, says researcher

description: A footpath home disappears beneath brown water. The other side is only a few meters away and someone has already crossed. Turning back means a long detour and you will be late. Would you wade through? This is the kind of everyday decision that flood safety advice must address.
title: People wade through floodwater because they underestimate danger—how to avoid risk

description: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. If glaciers border a lake, the water can melt the ice from underneath; furthermore, chunks of ice can break off and fall into the lake. The extent to which these processes influence the situation, compared with other factors, had not been sufficiently clarified at a global level until now.
title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss

description: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have advanced the ability to measure temperatures in materials subjected to extreme pressures at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), providing new insights into how materials behave under conditions relevant to national security and high-energy-density physics.
title: X-ray technique advances temperature measurements under extreme pressure

description: Mitochondria are essential components of the cells of most organisms, including humans. They are often referred to as the cell's powerhouses because they produce the energy needed for cellular functions. However, mitochondria originally evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells in the distant past.
title: Parasite protein expands understanding of how mitochondria build their ribosomes

description: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale.
title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale

description: El Niño has a reputation for being a skier's dream, bringing lots of snow to California's Sierra Nevada and the southern Rockies. Tahoe-area resorts were already seeing the effects in mid-November 2026 as several feet of snow fell and some resorts prepared to open early for the season. But El Niño's supercharged precipitation can spell trouble, too.
title: El Niño created a skiers' paradise in Chile—now it's Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies' turn

description: Among the thousands of chemicals used in daily life, toxicity information is available for only a small fraction. Much of this information comes from high-dose animal studies, which are costly, time-consuming and limited by species differences.
title: Practical organ-on-a-chip platform helps assess the toxicity of environmental chemicals

description: Researchers have identified two previously unreported strains of freshwater cyanobacteria capable of producing a potent neurotoxin that poses risks to people, pets, wildlife and water resources and that some scientists suspect may have contributed to previous animal deaths.
title: New sources of neurotoxin linked to algal blooms uncovered in Florida and Kansas

description: Bigger brains mean greater intelligence, or so conventional wisdom goes. After all, humans have much larger brains than most other animals and are generally considered the planet's most intelligent species.
title: Bumblebees challenge long-held beliefs about brain size and intelligence

description: Young love, honeymoon love, infatuation—these often feel spectacular. You have a burning need to be in constant contact, and you don't want to let that person out of your sight.
title: Is it genuine love—or obsessive passion? Kierkegaard, the father of existentialism, had some thoughts

description: The burning of fossil fuels such as coal, gas and oil is the primary driver of climate change, but clean energy strategies to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions do not systematically alleviate other environmental problems. In fact, some pathways add pressure on natural resources like land, water and minerals.
title: Clean energy choices shape environmental impacts beyond greenhouse gas emissions

description: Billionaire Warren Buffett announced this month he will donate $5.47 billion to four foundations associated with his family ahead of Thanksgiving. Similarly, various students in club organizations throughout Kansas are collecting food items to give to hungry families for the holiday.
title: Witnessing generosity from low-income donors more likely to elicit giving from observers, research finds

description: An international team of researchers is revealing the largest study to date detailing the wide range of insects, arachnids and other organisms that live in homes and other indoor environments across the United States and Canada. The researchers have compiled a database with more than 20,000 entries spanning more than 2,000 species found in these indoor ecosystems.
title: Spiders, beetles and one garage alligator: Largest study to date reveals wildlife sharing our indoor spaces

description: Researchers have a new capability for exploring some of the least understood regions of the ocean. Developed by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) in collaboration with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Deep Venture is a next-generation autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) for deep-ocean research, capable of supporting a wide range of scientific missions, from shallow coastal waters to the deepest places on Earth. It can withstand extreme pressure, rated for depths of up to 11,000 meters (about 6.83 mi), or full ocean depth.
title: Deep Venture: A new class of ocean exploration vehicle developed

description: A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday that he had used the firm's Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved math's greatest riddle

description: Computer chip manufacturing and lunar exploration seem like completely different worlds. Yet our latest research suggests the two may be more closely connected than expected.
title: A new way to extract oxygen from lunar soil could support bases on the moon

description: Nuclear fusion promises a source of energy by combining light atomic nuclei, the same process that powers the sun. To achieve fusion on Earth, scientists must heat a gas to extreme temperatures, creating a charged state of matter called plasma. Keeping this plasma hot and stable long enough for fusion energy production is one of the main challenges facing the technology.
title: Theory explains how fusion plasmas enter a state of improved energy confinement, solving a 40-year puzzle

description: As nature declines over time, it becomes easier to normalize an increasingly impoverished environment.
title: U.K.'s nature health check doesn't stack up in wildlife's favor—but volunteers are collecting plenty of crucial data

description: New research from NIHR School of Public Health Research, published in the Lancet Planetary Health, provides new insights into how taking action on climate can impact young people's climate change distress, mental health and well-being.
title: More worried, yet more hopeful: The paradox of young people's climate action

description: Killer whales, or orcas, are among the ocean's most formidable predators, hunting everything from fish and seals to other whales. But how and when these members of the dolphin family evolved into such effective hunters has long been something of a mystery.
title: Killer whales became fearsome predators long before scientists thought

description: In the desert, winter snow may seem like a temporary visitor, but its effects can last long after the snow melts. By supplying water to dry ecosystems, snowfall helps sustain biological soil crusts (biocrusts), thin living layers on the soil surface that play important roles in desert ecosystems.
title: How desert biocrusts respond to changing snow cover

description: Combining their skills in theory and experiment, Yale researchers have observed for the first time a type of energy-carrying composite particle move in a highly unexpected way. It's a finding that could lead to advances in quantum technologies, solar energy, LEDs and other optoelectronic technologies. The work is published in Nature Physics.
title: Excitons mimic light in atom-thin material, confirming decade-old quantum prediction

description: Stars in the night sky may look calm and unchanging, but some are in fact constantly "vibrating." Just as a musical instrument can sound several notes at once, a star can pulse in several modes simultaneously. By measuring minute changes in a star's brightness, astronomers can read these stellar vibrations and, in turn, probe the physical processes at work inside it.
title: Researchers trace shifting pulsation modes in δ Scuti star KIC 4737720

description: Venus is one of the most inhospitable environments in our solar system, with surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead and atmospheric pressure nearly 100 times greater than Earth's. Yet its surface may preserve clues to a time when the planet looked much more like Earth.
title: Venus-like conditions reveal how minerals could preserve traces of ancient water

description: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) has been the poster child of climate change, but another culprit could be flying just under the radar. Methane is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential approximately 84 times greater than that of CO₂ over a 20-year period. Fortunately, methane remains in the atmosphere for only about a decade, and reducing its emissions could provide rapid climate mitigation effects.
title: Tokyo's hidden methane: Survey pinpoints nearly 100 hot spots

description: For decades, researchers have assumed male bumblebees' contribution to hives consisted mainly of DNA. However, a new study finds that the males actually help incubate baby bumbles, and that with males' assistance, hives thrive. The study, published in the Royal Society Open Science journal, quantifies the beneficial effects of having male babysitters in the hive.
title: Male bumblebees contribute to nest care, challenging view that they only mate

description: A new study by Adelaide University researchers has found that the more often people perceived they had encountered misinformation, the less positive their views of Australian democracy tended to be. The experience-sampling study from the School of Psychology asked 123 eligible voters to track their perceived exposure to misinformation in the lead-up to the 2025 Australian federal election and measured whether this exposure influenced their attitudes and emotions toward the election.
title: Misinformation perception shapes support of democracy in Australia

description: Since 2021, the Mars Perseverance rover has been roaming Jezero Crater, gathering details about the red planet's geology and hints about its past. On its journey, the rover took close-up images of the Séítah formation, a nearly 4-billion-year-old layer of rock at the base of the crater.
title: Low-viscosity lavas reveal a key to Mars's past

description: Researchers from the University of the Sunshine Coast observed how a total of 959 consumers in the U.S., South Korea and Germany used mobile streaming services.
title: Mobile streaming habits offer global societal insights

description: Stars like our sun don't die quietly. In their final act, they swell into red giants, shed their outer layers into space and leave behind a glowing, often strikingly sculpted cloud of gas called a planetary nebula. That transformation is thought to take only a few thousand years, a blink in the life of a star, so catching one in the act is rare.
title: A star's last gasps: ALMA reveals a giant gas ring and budding hourglass around a star in transition

description: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) are the most important managed pollinator of agricultural crops globally. A study published Nov. 19 in the open-access journal PLOS Biology by Huoqing Zheng at Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China, and colleagues suggests that parasitic mites causing honey bee colony collapse have less reproductive success at high altitudes.
title: Low oxygen at high altitudes may protect honey bees from deadly parasites

description: A tangle of long, caramel-colored seaweed. That's what botanist A.H.S. Lucas found in 1935 while conducting research near Lord Howe Island, a World Heritage–listed site known for its unique biodiversity. After collecting some large adult specimens of this previously unidentified seaweed, Lucas named it Sargassum howeanum.
title: We found a seaweed that hadn't been spotted in 90 years—and discovered vast underwater forests

description: Rayon, the soft, breathable fabric many people have come to love, is often derived from wood pulp. Wood pulp is made by breaking wood down into its fibers, which can then be pressed into paper or spun into thread. Much of that pulp comes from plantations in Indonesia, where it becomes common household goods sold around the world: paper, tissue, packaging and, yes, clothing.
title: From paper to rayon: The wood pulp behind everyday goods is putting Indonesia's forests at risk

description: Superconductivity, the ability to carry current with no resistance, has been found in materials ranging from metals to oxides. Conventional Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) theory explains low-temperature metal superconductors well, but struggles with high-temperature oxide superconductors.
title: New model predicts critical temperature of superconductors

description: Is artificial intelligence (AI) finally coming for Australian jobs?
title: With AI blamed for mass layoffs, here's how we can ensure workers get a fairer deal

description: These glow-in-the-dark, googly-eyed fishes perform the biggest daily migration of any animal on the planet and are among the most abundant and important fishes in our oceans. But they are also among the most mysterious. Now, Australian researchers finally have access to a comprehensive guide to aid in the identification of Australian lanternfishes.
title: Illustrated guide shines a light on Australia's lanternfish

description: Jupiter's moon Europa is a world of scientific intrigue, with a global ocean believed to lie beneath its icy crust. Now, observations from W. M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea, Hawaiʻi Island, reveal something unexpected: the enormous, diffuse cloud of sodium surrounding Europa has remained remarkably stable across more than two decades of observations, despite the dynamic environment surrounding Jupiter.
title: Astronomers reveal the oceanic origin of Europa's sodium cloud

description: In 2016, biologist Sandra A. Binning and a group of young researchers traveled to Australia's Lizard Island Research Station, at the northern end of the Great Barrier Reef in the Coral Sea.
title: Reef fish aren't so vulnerable to ocean acidification, after all

description: Microscopic particles called nanoparticles hold promise for delivering cancer treatments directly to tumors, potentially making therapies more effective while sparing healthy cells. But a major obstacle stands in the way: Other cells in the body can intercept these tiny particles before they reach their intended targets.
title: Why nanoparticles struggle to reach ovarian cancer cells

description: In the business world, knowing the right people is often considered a passport to success. A well-connected professional can introduce colleagues to new clients, bring together experts from different departments or create collaborations that would otherwise never happen. But there is a catch: The people best positioned to connect others may also be the ones others are least inclined to trust.
title: The networking paradox: Knowing more people can make you less trustworthy

description: Accurate species delimitation is fundamental to biodiversity conservation, yet it remains a persistent challenge in species-rich plant groups, particularly conifers, where convergent evolution, gene flow and incomplete lineage sorting often obscure species boundaries.
title: Study reveals hidden evolutionary diversity in endangered white pines

description: For nearly three decades, scientists have struggled to explain one of the universe's most enduring mysteries: how a component known as dark energy is driving the accelerating expansion of the cosmos.
title: Dark energy may originate from known laws of particle physics

description: Four new studies show how Earth observation has become an everyday instrument for watching and protecting the continent's forests and green spaces, from a single city park to the whole of Europe.
title: What can satellites see when they look at Europe's forests?

description: Trapped within diamond's crystal lattice are tiny defects called nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, where a nitrogen atom sits beside an empty gap where a carbon atom should be. Because of their quantum spins, electrons trapped at these defects behave like tiny magnets, turning diamond into a highly sensitive detector for magnetic fields.
title: Spiraling spins bring coordinated quantum motion to diamond sensors

description: For those of us on Earth's surface, we reach for sunscreen when we want protection from the sun's radiation. That is because there are other "rays" that the atmosphere and the Earth's magnetic field keep out, like galactic cosmic radiation. Galactic cosmic rays are highly energetic particles found in space.
title: Space travel changes the brain's immune cells, but not behavior

description: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are materials that incorporate living organisms, such as bacteria, fungi or yeast, to perform specific functions. These organisms can produce substances, respond to signals from their surroundings or help repair damage to the material itself. Some organisms naturally possess properties that researchers can put to use. For example, certain bacteria produce cellulose, a substance that can be used to make clothing and textiles.
title: EU regulations could hold back innovation in living materials

description: A new study published in Environmental Research Letters finds that, despite experiencing rapid population growth, expanding economies and rising electricity demands over the past half century, the U.S. Northeast and Midwest have dramatically strengthened their resilience to severe drought through long-term investments in water efficiency, technological innovation and economic transformation.
title: Study finds decades of water-saving innovation helped Northeast and Midwest avoid potential drought crises

description: Researchers at Murdoch University have found the first evidence that artificially incubated southwestern snake-necked turtles can survive in the wild for more than a year after release, offering hope for struggling populations in Perth's urban wetlands.
title: Lab-hatched turtle survives in the wild, offering hope for Perth populations

description: Some spiral galaxies look heavier or more elongated on one side than the other. Why galaxies get lopsided is not fully understood. It could be due to collisions or gravitational tugs, uneven gas infall, or instabilities within the disk that drag the gas and stars off-center. In a new study, astronomers combined measurements of galaxies from 37 studies to create a big catalog and analyzed it to check for lopsidedness and its cause. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 10.
title: Why are some galaxies more lopsided than others? A catalog offers clues to the imbalance

description: A University of Sydney Ph.D. student has uncovered evidence that the Milky Way is unusual in terms of where its new stars are born compared with nearby galaxies.
title: Galactic shock: Discovery challenges our understanding of the Milky Way's structure

description: Researchers in the Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences (SEAS) have engineered an advancement in metasurface design and processing that now includes a built-in, intentionally designed antireflective coating—a potentially critical step toward greatly expanding the incorporation of metasurfaces into practical devices.
title: A two-layer flat lens uses nanoscale pillars to guard against unwanted reflections

description: The U.N.'s COP31 climate talks enter their endgame Friday, with countries sharply divided over a draft deal lacking any mention of planet-heating fossil fuels, threatening to push the negotiations into overtime.
title: UN climate talks enter crunch time with no deal in sight

description: World-famous hippopotamus Fiona has died after several failed attempts by vets to remove a woolly hat that she accidentally swallowed, the Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday.
title: Fiona the hippo dies after failed effort to remove swallowed hat

description: Researchers from the University of Nottingham, in collaboration with Syngenta and Keele University, have discovered how a commercial barley hybrid uses three complementary natural defenses to protect itself against aphids and the damaging viruses they spread. The findings could help breeders develop crops with stronger natural protection against pests and diseases.
title: Nature's multilayered defenses against crop pests and viruses revealed
